data.name: EveConsoleIsDownloadingNote
data.value: EVE Console is downloading the EVE game data it needs (the Static Data Export and Hoboleaks data) in the background. This can take a few minutes — item lookups, market pricing, and industry tools will fill in as it completes. You can watch progress on the SDE tab in Settings.
data.comment: Note in WelcomeWindow.

data.name: OnceThatFinishesRestartNote
data.value: Once that finishes, restart EVE Console. Some tools load their reference data when they first open, so a restart makes sure everything sees the freshly imported data.
data.comment: Note in WelcomeWindow.

data.name: ToPullInYourNote
data.value: To pull in your own characters and corporation data, add your ESI character tokens. The Settings window will open on the ESI Tokens tab next — click Add under Characters there to log in through EVE's SSO.
data.comment: Note in WelcomeWindow.

data.value: This copy was not set up by the installer, so it cannot update itself. Install {0} or later from the releases page.

data.name: UpdateAheadCheckFailed
data.value: Could not check for an update: {0}. Get {1} or later from the releases page.
data.comment: Status in the dialog shown when the database is newer than this copy of the app, when the update check failed. {0} is the error (in English, without its closing full stop), {1} the database's version. "The releases page" is the web page the dialog's "Releases page" button opens.

data.name: UpdateAheadCheckFailedNoReason
data.value: Could not check for an update: no reason given. Get {0} or later from the releases page.
data.comment: Status in the dialog shown when the database is newer than this copy of the app, when the update check failed without saying why. {0} is the database's version. "The releases page" is the web page the dialog's "Releases page" button opens.

data.name: UpdateAheadNoRelease
data.value: No newer release is out yet. {0} has not been released: the database was opened by a development build, or the release is still being published.
data.comment: Status in the dialog shown when the database is newer than this copy of the app, when no newer release exists. {0} is the database's version.

data.name: UpdateAheadReleaseTooOld
data.value: The newest release, {0}, is still older than this database ({1}), which was opened by a build that has not been released.
data.comment: Status in the dialog shown when the database is newer than this copy of the app. {0} is the newest release's version, {1} the database's version.

data.name: UpdateAheadAvailable
data.value: Version {0} is available. Updating installs it and restarts EVE Console on this database.
data.comment: Status in the dialog shown when the database is newer than this copy of the app, when a release that can open it exists. {0} is that release's version. EVE Console is the product name.

data.name: RecoveryReasonUnknown
data.comment: Database recovery dialog, under "REPORTED": shown in place of the reason the database could not be opened, when none was given.

data.name: VersionMismatchDatabaseAhead
data.value:
This database is at version {0}, and this client is {1}.
A newer build has already changed this database in ways this one knows nothing about, and schema changes only ever move forward.
Update this client to {0} or later.
data.comment: Shown at startup, and the app then stops, when the database was upgraded by a newer copy of the app. {0} is the database's version, {1} this copy's version. A "client" is one running copy of the app; a "build" is a version of it.

data.name: VersionMismatchWorkerBehind
data.value:
This database is at version {0}, and this client is {1}.
Another client is running the background processes on {0}, and only that client may change the schema. The changes this build expects have not been made, so much of it would not work.
Update the client running the background processes to {1}, or close it and start this one first so that it takes over and applies them.
data.comment: Shown at startup, and the app then stops, when another copy of the app runs the background processes on an older version. {0} is the database's (and that copy's) version, {1} this copy's version. A "client" is one running copy of the app; a "build" is a version of it.

data.name: VersionMismatchHeading
data.value: This build does not match the database
data.comment: Heading of the dialog shown with VersionMismatchWorkerBehind, before the app stops.
